_what: Measured runs, not estimates. peak_vram_gb is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated for the attempt that PRODUCED THE OUTPUT — not the first attempt tried.
_axes: Two axes are recorded, output_pixels and frames_per_chunk, and neither captures what actually decides feasibility: the largest single allocation. A 2K-to-4K job OOMed at 75.13 GB peak and succeeded at 74.93 GB, because the rung that fit asked in smaller pieces rather than for less. Read these as cost, never as a fit test.
_provenance: scripts/run_one.py writes records/measurements.jsonl; this file is generated from it. Cards vary: rows carry gpu_name and vram_total_gb, and _matching_runs refuses to mix cards more than 4 GB apart. Two rows are marked `corrected` in the ledger — they were written before the winning-attempt fix. **Refit of 2026-08-19 (three rows).** The H200 enters the table for the first time, with the first 8K time row it has ever held; two RTX PRO 6000 rows at window 85 join it. Their phase_peaks_gb are transcribed from the gate's own certification entries rather than read from the banked rows — the harness has never written that field, and the 8K row additionally lost its build and prefix to F-2026-08-19-35. Each row says so in its own note, and the manifests named there remain the primary source. Not admitted: three CANCELLED jobs and one pre-GPU refusal from the same day, which have no honest per-frame cost for the same reason no OOM row is included; and clip 2, which had not banked a row when the first half of this refit was cut — it has since delivered and is folded in as the fourth row, the first banked whole through the repaired attach path with its build identity aboard. **2026-08-20:** the hero's high-tiling row is appended -- the table's first, banked from the run-record of the job that lost its master to F-2026-08-20-39. Its memory fields are absent rather than transcribed, and the row says so itself.
_gaps: Rows are no longer uniform in their INPUT, and that is the sharpest edge in this table. The older rows came from a 320x180 source or a still, so the source's own decode and VAE-encode cost is absent from them; rows from 2026-08-14 onward came from a 2K source and carry it. Two rows at the same output_pixels can therefore differ in seconds_per_frame for a reason no recorded axis explains, and the ones without a heavy input read fast. temporal_overlap has never moved independently of a rung. batch_size has, but only at swapped/8.29 MP (windows 21 and 33), so everywhere else the window is still the rung's. No OOM row is included: a rung that OOMed has no honest cost. **Two rows at the same size, card, window and configuration now differ by 19% in seconds_per_frame** (2026-08-19, window 85 at 8.29 MP: 5.753 and 4.839). Both are unforced planner choices on the same clip with per-phase peaks identical to the hundredth, so the difference is not in what ran — it is host or data-centre variance, which this table has no axis for and §8b already marks time as asterisked. Read a single time row as one host's answer, never as the card's. **The H200 pair proves the same point on the other card and at 8K**: clip 1 and clip 2 measured 21.601 and 19.009 s/frame at identical size, window and configuration, with per-phase peaks matching to the hundredth — 13% apart with nothing differing but the host. Two cards, two sizes, the same lesson: this table's time axis has a host-shaped hole in it, and the honest reading of any single row is a bracket rather than a value. **tile_quality enters the table (2026-08-20).** Thirty-nine rows carry no tile_quality and every one of them was planned at `default` -- the lever is release-2 and the first job ever to ask for `high` is the row appended here. The estimator reads an absent value as `default`, which is a statement about this table's history rather than a guess, and rung 1 asserts it. **And the time rows are now keyed on kind: a single-frame row may never price a video, nor a video row a still.** Sixteen of the thirty-nine are stills, and the pixel window let them cross: at 9.4 MP the unkeyed pool spanned 4.6 to 86.4 s/frame, and because the estimator takes the max over comparable rows, an A40 video job was being priced by an 86.4 s/frame still. A still has no temporal window and no batch, so its one frame pays the whole per-frame setup a video amortises -- a different quantity sharing a name. Measured effect on a 600-frame 1080p->4K A40 job: 41.100 s/frame before, 34.438 after. **schedule enters the table (2026-08-20).** The first `balanced` row is banked, and its rate carries the overlap surcharge by construction: the schedule grew the final pass's temporal overlap to 16, so it computed frames a `max_window` run of the same clip would not. A max_window row at the same card and size will read faster and THAT DIFFERENCE IS THE SCHEDULE, not host spread — a distinction this table has already got wrong once in the other direction. Rows without `schedule` predate the lever and ran max_window. **Time keying changes here (amendment 6e, 2026-08-20).** New rows carry `seconds_per_frame_post_strip` with `tail_seconds` as its own column, never a bare rate: one clip measured cold-vs-warm put 365 s of pure strip inside a 'per-frame' rate, and the B200 pair's entire 17.9-to-21.7 s/frame spread was tail variance on two runs whose phases matched to a couple of seconds. Every OLDER row's `seconds_per_frame` is a raw rate containing both, and must not be compared with a post-strip one. A row whose `tail_seconds` is null is keyed but not yet separated -- an upper bound on compute, not the compute term.

THE FIRST tile_quality: high ROW IN THIS TABLE, and the reason F-2026-08-20-40 exists. The hero shot (00188, 4K source to 7680x4320, 192 frames) ran high tiling: decode moves from 6x4 tiles at 1392 px to 3x2 at 2648, seven passes of ~900 s each against ~120 s at the default, and the entire 2x wall lives there. Predicted 4147.4 s from a default-tiling H200 row wearing prediction_basis 'measured'; the attempt took 8922.9 s. Until this row existed the estimator had no high-tiling measurement to prefer, which is why the label was degraded to 'borrowed' rather than the number corrected -- deriving a 2x factor from one lost run would have been inventing a measurement to repair a mislabelled one. ARITHMETIC: 8922.9 s over 192 frames = 46.473 s/frame. The gate relayed 46.7, which implies 191 frames (8922.9 / 46.7 = 191.1); 46.473 is the figure derivable from the two facts on the record and is what is banked. The 0.5% discrepancy is filed rather than silently resolved. MEMORY FIELDS ARE ABSENT, NOT ZERO: this row is banked from the run-record's attempt seconds and the job's geometry. peak_vram_gb, phase_peaks_gb, window and chunk_size are not transcribed because the master was lost to F-2026-08-20-39 and this session cannot read the record directly. A time row needs seconds_per_frame and output_pixels; it is honest as a time row and must never be read as a memory row. Primary source: runs/2026-08-20/...T090719....json. WINDOW AND CHUNK ARE DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, and labelled as such. The planner is deterministic and tile_quality moves only the decode grid, never step 1's window budget: planning this exact geometry on this card yields window 29 / chunk 192 at BOTH tile qualities. It is corroborated rather than merely computed — the default-tiling row above at the same card, size and frame count BANKED window 29 from a real run. If the record is ever read directly and disagrees, the record wins and this row is corrected.

Read back from the run-record directly (runs/2026-08-20/01REAL20260820T09331000.json, build d19bc57), not relayed: every field here including the phase peaks is the record's own, which is what the F-36 corpus was built for. **THE RATE INCLUDES THE OVERLAP SURCHARGE BY CONSTRUCTION.** schedule=balanced kept the window at the card's maximum (85) and grew the FINAL pass's temporal overlap to 16 so no pass fell below the floor -- so this run computed overlapping frames a max_window run of the same clip would not. A future max_window row at this size and card WILL read faster, and the difference is the schedule, NOT host or data-centre spread. This table has already been misread that way once: two rows at window 85 differing 19% were attributed to host variance, and the honest reading of any single time row here is a bracket. Do not pool this row with max_window rows to argue about hosts. The formula's own vindication rides along: dit_sample predicted 93.00 against 93.01 measured, unforced, on a card that had never run video. One discrepancy filed rather than smoothed: the estimator predicted 7.808 s/frame at prediction_basis 'measured' and the run took 5.717 -- a 37% OVER-prediction, the opposite sign to F-2026-08-20-40's tiling case, and unexplained by any axis this table records. Also visible in the record: attempts[0] carries tile_quality: null and schedule: null because this ran on the pre-Build-A image; the attempt record now carries both, which is what lets a future row of this kind be keyed without reading the rationale.

THE B200's FIRST ROW, and the first banked under amendment 6e's keying. Read from runs/2026-08-20/01REAL20260820T14430200.json directly. **MEMORY: complete and honest.** peak 175.1 GiB with the full phase set, and the ceiling is vae_encode rather than dit_sample -- the first card in this table where it is, because w37 is the largest window any card has run and encode scales with it. Host peak 107.52 reproduces the H200's 107.1-107.5 across eleven records to within 0.4 GiB: host cost is geometry, card-independent, exactly like the VRAM side. **TIME: keyed, but NOT YET TAIL-SEPARATED, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise.** seconds_per_frame_post_strip = (3387.3 - 77.7)/192 = 17.238, with the strip (import 2.3 + prepare 75.4) removed per amendment 6a. tail_seconds is NULL because this run predates F-2026-08-20-44: it ran on build 9b06916, which had no tail stopwatch. So 17.238 still CONTAINS the drain, which is the very contamination 6e exists to remove -- the B200 pair's whole 17.9-to-21.7 spread was tail. Treat this rate as an upper bound on the compute term, never as the compute term. The first fully separable time row can only come from a Build B image. ARITHMETIC FILED, not smoothed: the gate relayed 17.9 s/frame, which implies 3436.8 s against the 3387.3 s the record's own attempt carries; 17.642 is the raw rate and 17.238 the post-strip one, and neither is 17.9. The record's figures are what is banked.

H200 IN-BAND COVERAGE, banked as PURE RECORD (CF via the gate, 2026-08-28). Read off records/runs/2026-08-28_01REAL20260828T14122300.json, job 5f614078, endpoint z182yaz5i5w0b8, DC US-GA-2. **THIS ROW DOES NOT MAKE `same_card` NON-EMPTY AND IS NOT MEANT TO.** It carries no bare `seconds_per_frame`, per amendment 6e, and `_timing_rows` (estimator.py:238) selects only on that field -- so like the B200 row before it, this row is invisible to every prediction. A known and ruled state, not an oversight: the visibility question is board item 7's. Writing a bare rate here would put a strip-removed rate in a pool of raw rates where `max()` over a single same-card row would make it the whole ETA, underestimating wall time by exactly the term removed -- item 7's failure inverted rather than avoided, on the gate that refuses. **THE RATE IS post-STRIP, NOT post-TAIL:** (161.4 - 18.9)/90 = 1.5833, strip = import 2.6 + prepare 16.3, per amendment 6a and the B200 row's precedent. The gate relayed 1.7744, which is (161.4 - 1.7)/90 -- the TAIL removed instead of the strip. Filed, not smoothed: every component is banked here so either term is re-derivable, and `tail_seconds` is its own column precisely so the rate need not carry it. Corroboration that the attempt's seconds include the strip: phase_seconds sum to 142.6 against an attempt of 161.4, a difference of 18.8 against a measured strip of 18.9. **AND THE DECOMPOSITION CLOSES, WHICH IS WHAT SETTLED THE RATE** (gate, 2026-08-28): phases 142.6 + strip 18.9 = 161.5 against an attempt of 161.4, so the residual is -0.1, rounding. There is therefore NO ROOM for tail_seconds outside the phases -- it is inside them, already counted. Subtracting it from the attempt as well would be double subtraction rather than a different convention, which is why post_strip does not net the tail and why the gate's 1.7744 was withdrawn rather than reconciled.
runs.why_pure_record: Banked as coverage on 2026-08-28 and ruled by CF not to make same_card non-empty. **THIS FIELD IS THE RULING; THIS ROW'S `note` DESCRIBES A MECHANISM THAT NO LONGER HOLDS.** The note says the row is invisible because `_timing_rows` selects only on `seconds_per_frame` — true when it was written, and time-model.md §0c (2026-08-31) removed exactly that blindness, so the selector now converts a post-strip row and would read this one. A row that is inert BY RULING must not depend on a bug to stay inert, which is why the ruling is a field a selector can read rather than a sentence in prose.

_schema: Every row carries `window` -- min(batch_size, chunk_size), the axis peak VRAM actually follows -- or is marked `unusable_for_fit` and skipped by _matching_runs. **This table did not record the window until 2026-08-15**: of 70 peaks taken before then only two carried it, so any run with a forced batch was unattributable. `window_source` says how each was recovered. 'rung defaults' means nothing was overridden, allowing for frames_per_chunk() clamping the chunk to a short clip. 'row note' and '_gaps note' mean the window was written in prose and had to be read back out by hand -- three rows depend on a sentence, which is exactly the fragility this column removes going forward. New rows must set window, batch_size, chunk_size and phase_peaks_gb (handler/phasewatch.py) as fields. Lever fields (tiling flags, tile sizes, blocks_to_swap, swap_io_components) were backfilled from the rung definitions on 2026-08-16, which is exact because a rung *is* those values; tile overlap is 128 on every historical row because it was never passed until that date.
